hypotheses.justification: The statement stays true for every real t. rhoC is a piecewise definition. If t ≤ params.phi, the value is 1/2. If params.phi < t ≤ params.theta, the value is t/2 - b1. If theta < t ≤ eta, the value is 1 + c2 + t. If eta < t ≤ tau, the value is a quadratic. If t > tau, the value is 0. The proof uses ht only through ht.1 (0 ≤ t), in the phase 2 and phase 3 branches. In those branches 0 ≤ t follows from the case hypotheses instead. The file already has `phi_nonneg : 0 ≤ params.phi` (line 662). In the phase 2 branch, hφ : ¬ t ≤ params.phi gives params.phi < t, so 0 ≤ t. In the phase 3 branch, theta < t and phi ≤ theta (`switchOrder.phi_le_theta`), so 0 ≤ t; `theta_lower_crude` (2/3 ≤ theta) also works. The phase 4 lemma `rhoC_phase4_nonneg` does not use ht at all. It derives 0 ≤ t from eta ≤ t and `four_fifths_lt_eta`. The first and last branches are `norm_num`. The upper bound t ≤ T is never used. So the proof becomes `rhoC_phase2_nonneg (le_of_lt (lt_of_le_of_lt phi_nonneg (not_le.mp hφ)))`, and similarly for phase 3, and the theorem holds for all t.
